clue.text: Funny old investigators with model for a bridgehead

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or peculiar, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

parts.note: G-men are FBI investigators in American slang
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: Some comic veteran detectives teaming up with a fashion model to seize a bridgehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' is the anagram signal for 'old'; G-men is American slang for FBI agents, and the Model T Ford supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodgment is a military foothold gained in enemy territory, which is what a bridgehead is.

clue.text: "Birds 2, bees 2, … _____, 1 down fall in love" (Cole Porter to Distel, possibly)

definitions.text: "Birds 2, bees 2, … _____, 1 down fall in love" (Cole Porter to Distel, possibly)

parts.words: "Birds 2, bees 2, … _____, 1 down fall in love" (Cole Porter to Distel, possibly)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Cole Porter's song lyric, where the numbers stand for the words of this answer and its partner light; Sacha Distel, a French crooner, recorded Porter songs

explanation.surface: A garbled quotation of a famous Cole Porter love song, as a singer might pass it on.
explanation.walkthrough: The lyric runs 'Birds do it, bees do it ... let's do it, let's fall in love'; the 2 and 1 down in the quotation stand for the two lights of this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing words of the song's refrain are exactly this phrase, which is also the song's title.

clue.text: See 1
It's warm as toast and warmer at home

parts.note: a muff is a fur tube that keeps the hands warm
in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A remark that something is as cosy as toast, and cosier still indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the toasted teacake being eaten warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffin is a bread roll served split, toasted and warm, so it is a warm thing eaten like toast.

clue.text: Showed Tarrant out by 45°

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV presenter called Tarrant demonstrating something at a 45-degree angle.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Tarrant is a British television presenter; 'out' rearranges the letters of SHOWED TARRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass bearing of 45 degrees points halfway between north and east, so going by 45° is heading that way.

clue.text: Make up about a hundred now

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hundred goes inside

parts.note: to make up for a wrong is to atone
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: An instruction to compensate with about a hundred right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without any waiting, a straightforward synonym pair.

clue.text: Time study requires putting one's foot down

parts.note: reading is study, as in reading a subject at university

explanation.surface: A bossy note that studying properly means being firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting one's foot down' looks like being firm, but here it is literal stepping.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading is stepping, literally placing a foot on the ground.

clue.text: Destructive feature coming up about one catalogue first

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following pieces
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
I is the Roman numeral for one
a list is a catalogue
I is used for first, as in a monarch numbered the first

explanation.surface: A destructive feature article appearing about a single catalogue, before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives I as in a monarch numbered the First; 'coming up' reads the feature upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nihilistic thinking rejects and seeks to tear down all institutions, so it is destructive in spirit.

clue.text: Monarch deprived of gold holds up an incinerator of rubber

indicators.note: holds means the shortened ruler goes around the next piece
deprived of means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: an emperor is a monarch
OR is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pyre is a pile for burning a body, so an incinerator gives A PYRE

explanation.surface: A penniless king holds up a burner made of rubber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deprived of' takes OR out of EMPEROR to leave EMPER; 'up' turns A PYRE into ERYPA, which EMPER 'holds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery paper is an abrasive paper used for rubbing surfaces smooth, so it is a rubber.

clue.text: Some trifling reverses in flavour nearly send us back-to-front

indicators.note: in means the turned letters go inside the next piece
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taste is flavour

indicators.note: reverses means the selected letters are turned to read backwards
some means only part of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A tasting of a trifle goes wrong and sends everyone the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RIFLI from tRIFLIng, which 'reverses' turns to ILFIR; 'nearly' cuts TASTE to TAST, and ILFIR goes 'in' it. 'send us' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Going tail first means going rear end foremost, the same as moving back-to-front.

clue.text: From other end Turks produced blast of lightning

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are worked into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turks at the far end generating a burst of lightning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From other end' looks like a reversal signal, but OTHER END TURKS is the anagram fodder and 'produced' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstroke is a stroke of lightning accompanied by thunder, a lightning blast.

clue.text: Girl with teeth next missing message?

indicators.note: missing means the letters of the message are taken out

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone

explanation.surface: A girl with her teeth, wondering whether a message is the next thing missing.
explanation.walkthrough: TEETHNEXT loses T, E, X and T in order, leaving a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethne is a female first name of Irish origin, so it is a girl.

clue.text: Wild youth ate fruit now

indicators.note: fruit means the product or result of something, so the letters are rearranged into what they yield

explanation.surface: A wild young person ate fruit just now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' looks like food the youth ate, but it signals the anagram; 'Wild' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without waiting at all.

clue.text: Block sitting with live music

parts.note: to jam is to block, as in a traffic jam
a session is a sitting, as of a court or committee

explanation.surface: A meeting to obstruct something, accompanied by a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam session is an informal gathering where musicians improvise live together.

clue.text: See 26
A revolutionary's yearning?

parts.note: Che Guevara is the famous revolutionary

explanation.surface: A question about what a revolutionary longs for.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a longing, as in an ache for home, so it means yearning.

clue.text: Former revolutionary's row is smothered by present operator

indicators.note: smothered by means the pieces are wrapped inside the next one

parts.note: Santa operates the business of delivering presents
a din is a row, a loud noise

explanation.surface: An old revolutionary's quarrel is drowned out by a current machine operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present operator' looks like someone working now, but it is Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sandinista was a member of the Nicaraguan revolutionary front of the 1970s and 80s.

clue.text: Compound where fabulous 22 and king get a bit of lunch in the morning

parts.note: 22 down is a bird, and the roc is a fabulous bird of legend
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: in means the bit of lunch goes inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, the morning
the opening bit of the word lunch

explanation.surface: Where a mythical bird and a king share a snack in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 refers to the answer to 22 down, a bird; the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend, hence 'fabulous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock alum is a chemical compound, a crystalline form of alum (potassium aluminium sulphate).

clue.text: They back not opening wine during meals

indicators.note: during means the trimmed wine sits inside the meals

parts.note: suppers are meals

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter is removed

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A dinner where people refuse to uncork the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' takes P from PORT to leave ORT, which goes 'during' SUPPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters are people who back someone or something.

clue.text: See 26
Being 18, change not now

parts.note: 18 across is supporters, and being a supporter is being pro

indicators.note: change means the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a cause urging change, but not just yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NOT into NTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal word meaning straight away, immediately.

clue.text: Hard look round wood with sailor for raw food

indicators.note: round means the stare goes around the following pieces

parts.note: a stare is a hard look
teak is a wood
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Glaring at a timber pile alongside a seaman to find something uncooked to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard look' is split apart by 'round', so the wood and the sailor sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is a dish of minced raw beef, a raw food.

clue.text: Girl doing time

definitions.meaning: British slang for a young woman
British rhyming slang (birdlime, time) for a prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Bird is slang both for a young woman and for a spell in prison, as in doing bird.

clue.text: See English agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: An instruction to meet a British secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, a literary synonym for see.

clue.text: Just the job, so I give out cards

parts.note: to deal is to give out cards

explanation.surface: A card player explaining that dealing suits them perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, and 'just the job' is a British idiom for exactly what is wanted.

clue.text: Sailor and don in trouble — they are dead

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman and a university lecturer get into difficulty and perish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'dead as a doornail'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doornails are proverbially dead, from the phrase 'as dead as a doornail', so they are things that are dead.

clue.text: As object not subject I appreciate the gift: 1down 2 5

parts.note: taken as written
the pronoun I as the subject of a sentence
used as an object, the first person pronoun becomes me
to like is to appreciate
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in thanking someone for a present.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to 1 down (let's do it) plus the words of 2 and 5, giving 'let's do it at once', which the proverb urges.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb urges acting immediately rather than waiting, the same as saying let's do it at once.

clue.text: (b) dry, just about — start of day

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: about means surrounding the following letter

parts.note: only means just, merely

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A wine note: dry, barely, at daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: '(b)' looks like a list label; as the second item, it means 'in second place'.
explanation.definitionFit: The label (b) marks the second point in a list, which is what secondly introduces.
